headline: Proteomics searches expand to proteoforms and dark proteome, with coverage gaps measured
label: Proteomics Search Space Expansion
summary: Foundation models, multi-enzyme DIA and rule-based peptide prioritization now extend assignable proteome space while exposing coverage biases.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the expansion of what proteomics searches can assign, paired with measurement of what those assignments cover. π-SPECFormer, a mass-spectrometry foundation model pre-trained on 291M spectra, targets dark-proteome decoding through de novo sequencing, spectrum clustering and modification detection. mE-DIA combines library-free, multi-enzyme DIA-MS with proteoform inference and a peptide mapper, reporting a 30% gain in protein identifications. On the coverage side, SeekNSee prioritizes proteotypic peptides via enzyme-aware in silico digestion with traceable rule-level scoring, and a proteoform-aware reanalysis of public bottom-up evidence finds basic-pI peptides depleted (OR 0.45). msiFlow 2.0 is a less directly aligned contribution to imaging workflows. What is new is the joint move toward proteoform-level resolution and measured coverage gaps, with scoring rules made traceable.
